body:
Reporter request (2026-11-23): **CamCraft starts Ollama itself, and shows its log.**
1. **Start Ollama.** When "Offline local (Ollama)" is chosen and nothing answers on its URL, but an `ollama` binary is installed (PATH, `/Applications/Ollama.app`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`), offer a **Start Ollama** button. It runs `ollama serve` as a child process, honours `OLLAMA_HOST` / `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` / `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` from a small settings group, and stops it when CamCraft exits (only the one CamCraft started). The panel text says clearly that CamCraft started it.
2. **Show the log.** A collapsible **Ollama log** with the last N lines of that server's stdout/stderr, for example `[GIN] 2026/11/23 - 20:16:01 | 200 | 28.083µs | 127.0.0.1 | GET "/api/version"`, so the user can see requests arrive, the model load and errors. When CamCraft did not start the server, show CamCraft's own request log for that endpoint instead (time, path, status, duration), with no prompt text by default.
3. Never start a server that listens beyond loopback unless the user set that on purpose.
Done means: from a Mac with Ollama installed but not running, the user can start it from the panel, see its log lines, and chat. A test covers the "already running" / "not installed" / "started by CamCraft" states.

Provider list additions (reporter, 2026-11-23):

1. **Label OpenAI so people recognise it.** Merge "OpenAI Responses" and "OpenAI Chat" into one entry labelled **"OpenAI (ChatGPT models)"**. Its help says that a ChatGPT subscription does not include API access, and that the key comes from platform.openai.com with billing (see #3781).
2. **Presets on the custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.** These are a name, a base URL and a key name, with no provider-specific code. Users pick one instead of typing a URL:

| Preset | Base URL | Note |
|---|---|---|
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | one key, many models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama, Mistral); test key on the maintainer's M5 |
| Groq | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | fast, low-cost open models |
| Mistral | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | EU provider |
| DeepSeek | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | low cost |
| xAI (Grok) | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | on request |
| LM Studio (local) | `http://localhost:1234/v1` | already in presets.rs, hidden |
| Unsloth Studio (local) | `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1` | already in presets.rs, hidden; reporter validates |
| llama.cpp llama-server (local) | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` | already in presets.rs, hidden; needs `--jinja` |
| vLLM (local) | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | self-hosted GPU servers |

   Verify each URL against the provider's current documentation when it is added. A preset's model list comes from its `/models` endpoint where one exists. Each preset needs a tool-calling check: not every model on these services supports tools, so fall back to read-only Q&A and say so.

3. **Later, if shops ask** (each needs its own sign-in and URL scheme, so they are separate issues): Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI. These let a company keep the chat under its own cloud contract and data rules.
